Ordinary morning guide to handler pairs
This page teaches what to practise

This page covers the first checks for the Companion Animal Travel Desk at Aurelia Skyways and shows why steady handling matters. New staff should keep their voice even, watch the animal closely, and confirm the paperwork before the crate moves forward. Good work here prevents delay, protects welfare, and keeps the handoff clear for the rest of the team.

Start with the crate and the animal together. Look for secure latches, clean bedding, and enough room for the pet to stand, turn, and settle without strain. <<FACT F070>> <<FACT F064>> If anything seems off, pause the process and bring in the senior coordinator before the check-in continues. For rabbits, treat the crate as a calm space rather than a holding area, and avoid rough handling or sudden noise. 

For dogs, the main point is readiness for travel, not speed. <<FACT F075>> After that, confirm the owner has followed the current route guidance and that the animal has water access as needed. Watch for signs of distress, but do not crowd the crate or rush the handoff. If a passenger like Ravi Park or Hugo Williams raises a concern, listen fully, repeat the plan in plain terms, and move to escalation only after a calm review. Stella, like any pet, should be handled with patience and steady routine.

Remember to check, listen, and act in order every time.
